dedupe_keys.name: realisation of flood protection measures for the city of prague climate adapt case study

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study describes how Prague built a flood control system on the Vltava after the floods of 1997 and 2002, the latter a 500-year event that caused about 1 billion euros of damage. Built in eight stages from 1997 to 2012, the system has about 19.3 km of fixed barriers, concrete walls and mobile barriers (6.9 km mobile) and valves in the sewer network, designed for the 2002 flow of 5,160 m3/s plus a 30 cm margin; a 2022 permit raised the Old Town section to the same level. Costs are put at 145.9 million euros (2013), and benefits are estimated for 20 to 500-year floods, exceeding costs from the 50-year event. Coverage is the city of Prague. The page is accessible online as free HTML on the Climate-ADAPT portal, published in 2023 and updated in 2026. Caveats: permits were slowed by land ownership and heritage rules, the grey system does not suit flash floods on small streams, and the 2013 flood showed that the Rokytka pumping station was too small. Simulation uses: design floods, damage estimates and barrier layout for flood defence and climate adaptation studies. Related records: ČHMÚ hydrology open data (data-chmi-czech-hydrology-open-data).
name: Realisation of flood protection measures for the city of Prague (Climate-ADAPT case study)
organisations: Povodí Vltavy (Vltava River Basin state enterprise)
outcomes: About 19.3 km of fixed and mobile barriers (6.9 km mobile) now protect most of Prague against a 500-year flood plus 30 cm; the system held in the 2013 flood, which exposed the undersized Rokytka pumping station.
provider: Climate-ADAPT (European Environment Agency), case study with Prague City Hall and CzechGlobe
resources_used: design flood of 2002 (5,160 m3/s, level 782 cm plus 30 cm margin)
